title: api-gateway: tune streaming proxy buffers and routing rules for tool/function-calls (OpenAI compat)
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: incidents and internal load tests showed increased tail latency and occasional truncated streaming responses for tool/function-calls when proxy buffers were saturated and routing favored high-throughput nodes that do not yet support precise OpenAI-compatible chunking semantics. This PR adjusts default streaming proxy buffer sizes, tightens routing rules for tool/function-calls, and adds compatibility fixes so chunked streaming responses preserve JSON boundaries for structured output and function calling. Changes include: 1) Increase default proxy streaming buffer from 64KB to 256KB (configurable via gateway.streaming.buffer_bytes) and add per-route override. 2) Add route policy 'prefer-low-latency-for-tool-calls' that pins function/tool-call requests to nodes with low serialization latency and explicit JSON-chunk alignment. 3) Implement backpressure metrics and counters (streaming.proxy.backpressure_count, streaming.proxy.buffer_bytes_used) and expose them to the console. 4) Improve OpenAI compatibility layer to ensure partial JSON objects are buffered until valid token boundaries are available and to emit final "done" chunks in the expected shape. 5) Update helm defaults and private installer config to include new tuning knobs. Backwards compatibility: changes are behind a runtime feature flag gateway.streaming.buffer_tuning=false by default; rolling the flag enables the tuned behavior. Rollout plan: canary to 5% of traffic for 48h with increased logging, then 25% for 24h, then full rollout if metrics stable. Linear: ENG-6123. Testing: unit tests for buffer behavior, integration tests for streaming tool-calls (ensures JSON integrity for structured outputs), end-to-end load test results attached. Risk: increasing buffer sizes affects memory footprint on proxy pods; mitigated by per-node caps and autoscaler thresholds. See release_notes for user-facing impact and recommended operators settings.

release_notes: Increase default proxy streaming buffer to improve streaming stability for large structured outputs and tool/function calls; new route policy to prefer low-latency nodes for function/tool-calls; added observability for proxy backpressure. Feature controlled by gateway.streaming.buffer_tuning flag; default off. Operators should review proxy memory settings before enabling in high-concurrency clusters.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: higher proxy memory usage when buffers increased. Mitigation: per-node caps, feature flag off by default, staged rollout with canary, updated autoscaler thresholds and docs.
notes_for_ops: To enable tuned behavior set gateway.streaming.buffer_tuning=true and ensure gateway.node_memory_cap_mb >= 512. Helm value: gateway.streaming.buffer_bytes (default 262144). Monitor streaming.proxy.backpressure_count and proxy memory before full rollout.
